sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221], with operating income growing faster at 20.5% [F223].
The shape is a steady compounding rather than a step change: growth held between 13.6% and 17.8% in every year except FY2023, when it slowed to 6.9% [D152][D311][D472].

The FY2023 slowdown came as Intelligent Cloud and Productivity and Business Processes grew while More Personal Computing declined on Windows and Devices [P39], and operating income growth fell to 6.2% that year [D312].
FY2026 was the strongest recent year, with revenue up 17.8% [D472] driven by Microsoft Cloud, Azure within Intelligent Cloud, and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [P17].
Microsoft Cloud reached $214.4 billion, or 64.6% of revenue, in FY2026 [S24][D566], up from 41.1% in FY2021 [D553].
Cloud contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% revenue growth in FY2026 [D568][D472], and Server products and cloud services alone added 11.0pp [D642].
Server products and cloud services revenue rose 31% on Azure and other cloud services growth of 41%, with server products up 1% [P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added 5.1pp [D649], growing 16% on Microsoft 365 Copilot and E5 revenue per user and 6% seat growth [P14].
Operating leverage is strong: incremental operating margin was 53.3% in FY2026 [D498], with revenue growth exceeding operating-cost growth by 10.3pp [D499].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against net income growth of 31.3% [D476][D474], a small gap because the diluted share count fell only 0.2% [D493].
Operating margin reached a window high of 46.8% in FY2026 [F50][D974], 5.1pp above the 41.7% window median [D975] and 16.7pp above the FY2017 low of 30.1% [D973].
Gross margin, by contrast, slipped to 67.9% [F30], below its 68.2% median [D981] and 1.9pp under the FY2024 high of 69.8% [D980].
The FY2026 operating margin rose 1.2pp [D487] despite cost of revenue taking 0.9pp off margin [D500], while R&D added 0.8pp and other lines 1.2pp [D501][D502].
The gross-margin pressure is stated: Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
Net margin jumped 4.2pp to 40.3% [D488][F70], helped by $6.5 billion of net gains on OpenAI investments in other income [P7].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $182.9 billion in FY2026 [D477][F100], or 55.1% of revenue [D457], while free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion [D478][F120].
Free cash flow was only 0.50x net income in FY2026 [D460], a window low against a 0.91x median [D988][D990], and its 20.2% margin is the window low [D982].

The gap is capital intensity: capex reached $115.9 billion, 34.9% of revenue [F110][D455], and 3.38x D&A [D461], with investing cash use up $66.9 billion mainly on a $51.4 billion increase in property and equipment additions [P1].
Operating cash flow growth itself came from higher cash received from customers and lower income tax payments, partly offset by higher supplier payments [P1].
Net cash stood at $72.9 billion in FY2026 [D465], or 22.0% of revenue [D466], with total debt down 6.6% to $40.3 billion [D495][D464].
That net cash position ranks in the 83rd percentile against six software peers, whose median is -7.2% of revenue [D1006][D1007].
Liquidity is thinner than it once was: the current ratio of 1.23x is the window low [F200][D991], against a 1.93x median [D993].
Buybacks and dividends of $48.7 billion consumed 72.7% of free cash flow in FY2026 [D467][D468], with $22.3 billion of repurchases and $26.4 billion of dividends [X147][X157].
Return on average equity of 34.0% [D471] sits at the peer median of 38.8% [D1011], reflecting the large equity base of $442.4 billion [F220].
The main flag is cash conversion: free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026 [R1][D406][D460], and at 0.50x in FY2026 it is far under the 1.90x peer median [D1008][D1009].

This is a capex-cycle effect rather than an earnings-quality problem, since operating cash flow still covered net income 1.37x [D459], but it persists as long as AI infrastructure spending grows faster than revenue.

The FY2017 recasts in pretax income, tax and receivables [R2][R3][R4] are low-severity data-quality items that do not affect any conclusion here, and the product-member overlap [R5] means segment members should not be summed.

Free cash flow margin: a move back above the 30.3% window median [D984] would confirm the capex cycle is easing; a further decline below the 20.2% low [D982] would extend the trend, visible in the FY2027 cash flow statement.

Operating margin: holding above the 46.8% window high [D974] would confirm continued operating leverage, while a drop below the 41.7% median [D975] would reverse it, shown in the FY2027 income statement.

Gross margin: recovery above the 68.2% median [D981] would signal AI infrastructure costs are being absorbed, whereas staying below the 67.9% FY2026 level [F30] would confirm the mix drag described in the Intelligent Cloud discussion [P11].
Capex against D&A: a ratio below the 3.38x FY2026 level [D461] would suggest investment intensity is normalising, reported in the FY2027 cash flow statement.
